concepts.def: Magnet made by current in a coil.
Coil of wire with a magnetic field.
Iron bar inside coil; boosts strength.
Electromagnet rings a bell when pressed.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A simple electromagnet:

1. Wrap a wire around an iron nail in a coil.
2. Connect to a battery.
3. Current flows - the nail becomes a magnet!

Disconnect the battery, and it stops being magnetic.

Unlike a normal magnet, an electromagnet is switchable.

To boost an electromagnet:

More turns in the coil.
More current through the wire.
Iron core instead of plastic.

Stronger electromagnets can lift heavier objects - scrapyard cranes carry whole car wrecks!

Electromagnets are everywhere:

Scrapyard cranes - pick up and drop iron with a switch.
Doorbells - magnetic plunger hits a bell.
Electric motors - in fans, drills, trains.
Maglev trains - float above the track on magnets.
Loudspeakers - vibrate cones to make sound.
